collections.title: USA – states
collections.intro: Every US state has its own design. Whether a state requires a front plate is a clue on its own: if you can see a plate on the front of a car, it narrows the state down.

items.name: Alabama
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

In newer footage yellow design shows up more often (late 2021 release) and more greeny plate shows up more often in older footage.

items.name: Alaska
items.note:
Front plates are required.

In newer footage you can see additional designs but yellow plate is by far the most prevalent.

items.name: Arizona
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Very distinctive purple patch on the plate.

items.name: Arkansas
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Gotta look for that maroon text in top center.

items.name: California
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Sometimes you can make out a bit of red in top center but most of the time you will just see plain white plate.

items.name: Colorado
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Dark green at the top.

items.name: Connecticut
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Connecticut plates are similar to other plates in the region (e.g. Illinois, Minnesota, Iowa) so consider other clues before making your guess.

items.name: Delaware
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Very distinctive gold mixed with dark blue.

items.name: Florida
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Remember to look for green around peach. That differentiate Florida's plate from Georgia one.

items.name: Georgia
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Florida's plate might look similar to Georgia's white plate, but Florida plate is green around the peach while Georgia's plate is white.

items.name: Hawaii
items.note:
Front plates are required.

You often might make out the arc pattern through the blur.

items.name: Idaho
items.note:
Front plates are required.

I call it Paraguayan flag plate.

items.name: Illinois
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Illinois plates are similar to other plates in the region (e.g. Connecticut, Iowa) so consider other clues before making your guess. Also, maroon text often shows up on the plate help you differentiate from CT and IA.

items.name: Indiana
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Even though "In God We Trust" plate is not a standard issue, it is very common in Indiana and deep blue part on the left of the plate is very distinctive. Standard issue plate is much harder to spot but look for a bit of brown in bottom center alongside the light blue in the top.

items.name: Iowa
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Faded green on the bottom of the standard plate is very distinctive for easy Iowa guess just don't confuse it with Maine where green is of darker shade.

Iowa's blue/white plates are similar to other plates in the region (e.g. Illinois, Connecticut, Minnesota) so consider other clues before making your guess.

items.name: Kansas
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Might be similar to other plates especially to old RI plate, but with reverse color pattern.

items.name: Kentucky
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Kentucky plate looks similar to Michigan plate, but blue part should be bigger than on Michigan's plate.

items.name: Louisiana
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Colors of this plate seems to be bleaker than the image suggests so it is not that easy to spot it. Look for that fade pinkish/yellowish bottom with possibly a bit of red in top center. Honestly, this plate often looks plain white. In older footage or on older cars colors seems to be more distinctive.

items.name: Maine
items.note:
Front plates are required.

You might confuse it with Iowa's standard issue so make sure the green is very deep.

items.name: Maryland
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Look for that distinctive red/brown part in bottom center.

items.name: Massachusetts
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Red text is usually visible through the blur.

items.name: Michigan
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

white/blue design is similar to Kentucky plate so consider other clues before making a guess. Blue part on Michigan plate usually shows up smaller than Kentucky one.

Yellow plate with a bridge shows up less often but it's distinctive enough to immediately guess Michigan.

items.name: Minnesota
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Top blue part is smaller compared to Illinois and Connecticut. Also look for that bit of blue in bottom center to differentiate it from Iowa. Sticker in bottom right might help you as well.

items.name: Mississippi
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

White plate shows up in newer footage (2024 onwards). If you're lucky dark blue dot shows up in the middle of the plate, depending on the lighting the effect might be strong or very subtle.

2019-2023 plate shows up through blur as two big patches of light brown divided by white section in the middle. You can often see it in parking lots because they usually have older footage.

items.name: Missouri
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Tough plate to spot quickly but look for that thin red and blue strips. Between the two red is definitely easier to spot initially. Sticker of varying color is usually placed dead center and shows up through the blur.

items.name: Montana
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Montana might be the least consistent state in terms of plates. It has one of the highest varieties of license plate designs including many specialty/charity plates and free replica bases of older designs. The plain dark blue one is the default one, but you don't see it as often as default plates in other states. The best advice for Montana I can give is that if it seems like every car has a different plate than there is a high chance it's Montana.

items.name: Nebraska
items.note:
Front plates are required.

First plate is white with dark blue and yellow top strip. Can be confused with West Virginia's plate so look for other clues as well.

2nd plate shows up in new footage. Through the blur looks white, but sometimes you can see 1 or 2 dark blue spots in the middle.

items.name: Nevada
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Pretty easy to spot and remember, blue takes a big portion of the plate with bottom yellow strip.

items.name: New Hampshire
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Look for patch of green on the right side.

items.name: New Jersey
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Very common and very easy to spot.

items.name: New Mexico
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Yellow plate is more common, but turquoise plate is seen a lot as well.

items.name: New York
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Both variants are almost equally shown on street view.

items.name: North Carolina
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Red text shows up at the bottom while feint blue shows up in the middle of the plate.

items.name: North Dakota
items.note:
Front plates are required.

More vivid blue and orange bottom strip make it easy to differentiate it from Nevada's plate.

items.name: Ohio
items.note:
Front plates are required.

In older footage look for the 2nd design.

items.name: Oklahoma
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

This plate shows up through the blur as light blue all around white center.

items.name: Oregon
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Tree shows up as a big green oval. Very distinctive.

items.name: Pennsylvania
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Blue-white-yellow pattern is very easy to remember.

items.name: Rhode Island
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Look for that feint blue wave pattern when looking for RI plate.

New RI plate might appear all blue on the street view. Introduced in 2023 so look for it in new coverage.

items.name: South Carolina
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Sometimes both blue strips converge and make it harder to distinguish this plate from Montana and Tennessee, but usually white middle divides them well.

items.name: South Dakota
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Blue on top of brown/grey.

items.name: Tennessee
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Similar to Montana's plate but much more common to see in Tennessee.

items.name: Texas
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Sometimes you can see black text coming through but often shows up as a plain white plate.

items.name: Utah
items.note:
Front plates are required.

The Arch plate is extremely common and easy to spot, but 2nd plate shows up decent amount as well.

items.name: Vermont
items.note:
Front plates are required.

One of the easier plates to remember. Full green plate.

items.name: Virginia
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Plain white plate. Possible stickers in both top corners of the plate.

items.name: Washington
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Blue shows up in very light color and sometimes you can even see a bit of red text in top left.

items.name: Washington D.C.
items.note:
Front plates are required.

This plate is only being use in the Washington City.

Unfortunately, this plate is hard to spot and often shows up as plain white.

items.name: West Virginia
items.note:
Front plates are not required.

Can be confused with Nebraska's plate so look for that hard to spot feint yellow at the bottom of the plate as well as other clues. Also, West Virginia sticker should be in one of the bottom corners while Nebraska's sticker is in top right corner.

items.name: Wisconsin
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Red text in top left often shows up through the blur.

items.name: Wyoming
items.note:
Front plates are required.

Wyoming doesn't have a lot of street view coverage, but if you do end up in Wyoming this plate is easy to spot.

collections.title: Canada – provinces & territories
collections.intro: Each province has its own plate; several are recognisable through the blur.

items.name: Alberta
items.note:
Alberta plates are white and have red on the left and right side.

Front plates not required.

items.name: British Columbia
items.note:
British Columbia license plates are mostly white with green in the middle bottom.

Front plates required.

items.name: Manitoba
items.note:
Manitoba license plates are white with green on the far left and right side. A small yellow part can often be seen too at the bottom.

Front plates required.

items.name: New Brunswick
items.note:
New Brunswick license plates are white with red on the left and right side and a little bit of blue on the top which can be hard to spot.

NOTE: Since 2019, front plates are no longer required in New Brunswick. However, you should still expect to see them in older coverage. As well, all commercial vehicles in Newfoundland and Labrador are required to use front plates, and so it is possible to see them on vans and pickup trucks.

items.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
items.note:
Newfoundland and Labrador license plates are white with blue on the left and right side. Sometimes it has square yellow and red parts in the bottom corners.

License plates in Labrador are very rare to see, pretty much only found in Happy Valley-Goose Bay. Churchill Falls and a few spots in Labrador City.

Front plates not required.

items.name: Northwest Territories
items.note:
Northwest Territories plates have a cool polar bear shape, you can tell by the head sticking out on the top right.

Front plates not required.

items.name: Nova Scotia
items.note:
Nova Scotia license plates are white with blue in the middle and a little bit of blue around it sometimes.

Front plates not required.

items.name: Ontario
items.note:
Ontario license plates are most commonly white with blue on the left and right side.

Front plates required.

items.name: Prince Edward Island
items.note:
Prince Edward Island license plates are either white with green in the middle and red in the left corner. Or just white with a bit of black and a smaller red part in the corners. Just check if it has those red corners and it should be a PEI plate.

Front plates not required.

items.name: Quebec
items.note:
Quebec license plates are white with blue on the left and right side, the blue is a bit darker than the blue Ontario and Nova Scotia use.

Front plates not required.

items.name: Saskatchewan
items.note:
Saskatchewan license plates are white with green on the left and right side, the plate can often look more green than white. Also sometimes also has a bit of orange in the middle.

Front plates not required.

items.name: Yukon
items.note:
Yukon license plates are white with blue on the bottom left and right side with red between the blue. Also has a bit of orange on the left side.

Front plates not required.

collections.title: Mexico – states
collections.intro: Mexican states issue several designs each (old and new). Colour scheme is what survives the blur.

items.name: Aguascalientes
items.note: This plate features a thin orange stripe along the top and another along the bottom, making it relatively straightforward to identify among Mexican state plates. The center of the plate is white, with a faint round symbol visible in the background. Note that this is an older plate design, so you will mostly encounter it in older Street View coverage. The vast majority of plates from this state are generation 3.

items.name: Baja California
items.note: This plate is characterized by a blue stripe at the top and a light-blue center. The bottom typically displays a green stripe. In short, the overall color scheme is blue and green. Occasionally, a distinct dot is visible on the left side of the plate.

items.name: Baja California
items.note: This plate features an orange stripe at the top and a light-blue center. The bottom typically displays a green stripe. Overall, the color scheme combines orange, blue, and green. As with the other Baja California variant, a distinct dot is occasionally visible on the left side of the plate.

items.name: Baja California
items.note: This plate features two thick red stripes, one along the top and one along the bottom. It is the newest Baja California design, introduced in 2022, and is predominantly found in generation 4 coverage. If you're exploring recent Street View imagery of Baja California, this is the plate you'll most commonly encounter.

items.name: Baja California Sur
items.note: This plate is easily recognizable by its very thick orange stripe running along the top, making it one of the more straightforward plates to identify among Mexican states.

items.name: Baja California Sur
items.note: This plate is easily recognizable by its very thick purple stripe running along the top, making it one of the more straightforward plates to identify among Mexican states.

items.name: Campeche
items.note: This plate features a multicolored stripe along the bottom, displaying a alternating array of colors. When the plate is unblurred, the stripe reveals a distinctive cityscape motif made up of small houses in various colors. It can be tricky to identify at a glance, but a good rule of thumb is: if you spot a white plate with a heavily multicolored bottom stripe, it is very likely from Campeche.

items.name: Chiapas
items.note: This plate is white with a distinctive colored corner on each of its four corners: yellow or orange on the upper left, green on the upper right, red on the lower left, and blue on the lower right. This four-color corner pattern makes it one of the most unique and easily recognizable plates among all Mexican states.

items.name: Chihuahua
items.note: This plate is predominantly white, with a thick blue stripe running along the bottom. The blue band is centered at the lower portion of the plate and is quite clearly visible even from a distance. The rest of the plate is plain white with no other notable color elements.

items.name: Chihuahua
items.note: This plate features a thick red stripe along the top, paired with a much thinner red line along the bottom. The contrast between the bold upper stripe and the subtle lower line is a useful detail to keep in mind when identifying this plate.

items.name: Coahuila
items.note: This is a relatively recent plate design, introduced in 2022, and is characterized by a thick black stripe along the bottom. It is commonly encountered in the newer Street View coverage of Coahuila.

items.name: Colima
items.note: This is an older Colima plate design, but it appears frequently in the older Street View coverage of the state. The plate features a brown stripe on the bottom left and a green stripe on the bottom right. When the plate is blurred, these two stripes appear as a brown triangle and a green triangle, which can still serve as a useful identifying clue even at low resolution.

items.name: Colima
items.note: This is arguably one of the most recognizable Mexican state plates. It features a stripe along the bottom divided into the three colors of the Mexican flag: green on the left, white in the middle, and red on the right. Even when the plate is blurred, this tricolor band remains clearly visible, making it exceptionally easy to identify at a glance.

items.name: Durango
items.note: This is the newest Durango plate design, introduced in 2023, and is frequently found unblurred in Street View. Its most useful identifying feature is visible even when blurred: two orange dots, one on the bottom left and one on the bottom right of the plate. This plate is very common in the latest Street View coverage of Durango.

items.name: Durango
items.note: This is an older Durango plate design, most commonly encountered in older Street View coverage, though it occasionally appears unblurred in more recent imagery as well. When blurred, the key identifying features are a red background in the center and a green stripe along the bottom.

items.name: Durango
items.note: This white plate features a distinctive thin striped line along the bottom, made up of three colors in the following order: yellow, blue, and purple. Once you memorize this specific color sequence, the plate becomes very easy to identify. The combination is quite unique among Mexican state plates, making it one of the more memorable designs.

items.name: Estado de México
items.note: This plate is predominantly found in the older Street View coverage of Estado de México but also can be seen in the new coverage. It has a bluish background with two red stripes: a thicker one along the top and a thinner one along the bottom. The combination of the blue background and dual red stripes makes it one of the easier plates to identify with confidence.

items.name: Guanajuato
items.note: This plate has a light-blue background with a thin red stripe. It is an older design, so it is predominantly found in the older Street View coverage of Guanajuato.

items.name: Guerrero
items.note: Introduced in 2022, this plate is straightforward to spot in the newer Street View coverage of Guerrero. When blurred, its most recognizable feature is a red dot on the bottom left and another on the bottom right, making it relatively easy to identify even at low resolution.

items.name: Guerrero
items.note: This older Guerrero plate features yellow borders and a thick orange stripe along the bottom. It is predominantly found in the older Street View coverage of Guerrero.

items.name: Hidalgo
items.note: This is the newest Hidalgo plate design, introduced in 2023. When blurred, its key identifying feature is a thick dark red stripe along the bottom, which can sometimes appear purple depending on the image quality. This plate is widespread throughout the newer Street View coverage of Hidalgo.

items.name: Jalisco
items.note: Jalisco has two recent plate designs one from 2019 and one from 2023 which are very similar to each other. Both share the same key identifying feature: a small thick stripe along the top of an otherwise white plate. When blurred, this stripe can appear either dark blue or dark green depending on the image. If you spot a white plate with a narrow but prominent top stripe in one of these dark tones, Jalisco is a strong guess.

items.name: Jalisco
items.note: This is the older Jalisco plate design, predominantly found in the older Street View coverage of the state. It is one of the easier plates to recognize and remember, as it has a distinctly yellow top half and a blue bottom half, making it stand out clearly even in lower quality imagery.

items.name: Michoacán
items.note: This is the newest Michoacán plate design, introduced in 2022. Its most distinctive feature is a very thick stripe along the top, which can appear either dark red or purple depending on image quality. This plate is widely encountered throughout the newer Street View coverage of Michoacán.

items.name: Morelos
items.note: Morelos has two recent plate designs one from 2019 and one from 2022 which are very similar to each other. When blurred, both appear as a white plate with a large red dot on the bottom right. Once you know to look for that red dot on the right side, this plate becomes quite easy to identify.

items.name: Nayarit
items.note: This is the newest Nayarit plate design, introduced in 2022. It features a fairly thick multicolored stripe along the bottom, which can be tricky to identify when blurred. The key is to memorize the color order: light orange on the left, followed by blue and red in the middle, and green on the right. Remembering that the green is always on the right and the light orange always on the left is the most reliable way to distinguish this plate from others.

items.name: Nayarit
items.note: This is the oldest Nayarit plate design and quite distinctive. When blurred, it displays a prominent red triangle on the right side, making it relatively easy to identify at a glance. This plate is found exclusively in the older Street View coverage of Nayarit.

items.name: Nayarit
items.note: Nayarit has two older plate designs, both featuring a thin purple stripe along the bottom. The earliest version, released in 2016, includes a mountain scene in the background, and when blurred its purple stripe takes on an unusual triangular shape. The second version, released in 2017, is simpler, displaying just a plain thin purple line at the bottom with no background imagery. Both designs are predominantly found in Street View coverage from 2016 to 2020.

items.name: Nuevo León
items.note: This plate is entirely white with no notable color elements, making it one of the plainest Mexican state plates. Even when blurred, faint black text remains visible in the center. Its stark, minimalist appearance makes it relatively straightforward to recognize once you are familiar with it.

items.name: Puebla
items.note: This is the newest Puebla plate design, introduced in 2020, and is widely found throughout the recent Street View coverage of the state. The plate is white with a thick purple or dark red stripe that begins roughly in the middle of the plate and extends to the right. This distinctive half-stripe design makes it quite easy to recognize once you know what to look for.

items.name: Querétaro
items.note: This is the newest Querétaro plate design, introduced in 2022, and is widely found throughout the recent Street View coverage of the state. The plate is white with blue accents. When blurred, its most recognizable feature is a dark blue dot on the top left and another on the bottom right, creating a diagonal pattern that makes it quite easy to identify.

items.name: Quintana Roo
items.note: This older Quintana Roo plate was introduced in 2011 and used until 2013. When blurred, it shows an orange stripe along with a black dot in the center. As expected given its age, it is found exclusively in the older Street View coverage of Quintana Roo.

items.name: San Luis Potosí
items.note: San Luis Potosí has two plate versions one from 2016 and one from 2019 which are very similar and appear identical when blurred. Both designs are found across old and new Street View coverage of the state. The plate is white with a thick green stripe along the top, though notably the green does not extend all the way to the left edge, leaving a small white gap on the left side. This partial top stripe is the key detail to remember when identifying this plate.

items.name: Sinaloa
items.note: In contrast to the newer design, this older Sinaloa plate is very easy to recognize. When blurred, a large red dot appears prominently in the center of the plate, giving it a striking resemblance to the Japanese flag. This design dates back to 2006 and was used until 2011, so it is only found in the oldest Street View coverage of Sinaloa.

items.name: Sinaloa
items.note: This is arguably the hardest Mexican state plate to identify. The plate is entirely white with only a very thin red stripe along the bottom. When blurred, it appears as an almost completely white plate with just a faint hint of red at the bottom edge. Even if the red is barely visible, that subtle touch of color at the bottom is enough to confidently identify it as a Sinaloa plate.

items.name: Sonora
items.note: This is an older Sonora plate design, used approximately from 2014 to 2017, and commonly found in the older Street View coverage of the state. The plate is white with a very thin purple stripe along the bottom and a large orange dot on the right side. The combination of purple at the bottom and a prominent orange dot is the key detail to remember if you spot both of these features together, it is definitively a Sonora plate.

items.name: Tamaulipas
items.note: This plate was introduced in 2019 and is white with a multicolored stripe along the bottom. The bottom line can be ambiguous, but the key pattern to remember is blue on the left and green in the middle and on the right. Even when blurred, keeping that simple color order in mind blue left, green right is enough to identify this plate with confidence.

items.name: Tamaulipas
items.note: This is the newest Tamaulipas plate design, introduced in 2022, and is widely found throughout the current Street View coverage of the state. The plate is predominantly white and blue. When blurred, it displays a thick blue stripe along the bottom that appears to be split by a small white dot in the center. This uniquely shaped blue stripe makes the plate quite easy to identify once you know what to look for.

items.name: Tamaulipas
items.note: This is the most recent Tamaulipas plate design, introduced in 2023, and is widely found throughout the current Street View coverage of the state. The plate is predominantly white and red. When blurred, it displays a thick red stripe along the bottom with a small black dot on the left side. That combination a red bottom stripe with a black dot on the left is the key detail that distinguishes it from the other mexican plates designs.

items.name: Tlaxcala
items.note: This is the newest Tlaxcala plate design and is widely found throughout the current Street View coverage of the state. The plate is predominantly white and purple. When blurred, it displays a thick purple stripe along the bottom with a dark blue section within it. The key distinguishing detail is a dark blue dot in the middle of that stripe so the overall pattern to remember is a purple bottom stripe with a dark blue dot at its center.

items.name: Veracruz
items.note: This is an older Veracruz plate, used approximately from 2015 to 2017, and commonly found throughout the older Street View coverage of the state. When blurred, it displays a multicolored stripe along the bottom in the following order: green and yellow on the left, a visible orange dot in the middle, and a yellowish or green tone on the right. This plate is frequently seen unblurred in Street View, making it one of the easier ones to identify with confidence.

items.name: Veracruz
items.note: This is a very old Veracruz plate design, used from 2011 to 2017, and commonly found throughout the older Street View coverage of the state. It was specifically issued for private trucks. When blurred, the most distinctive feature is a green stripe along the bottom with rounded shapes resembling hills. As with the other old Veracruz design, this plate is frequently seen unblurred in Street View, making it straightforward to identify.

items.name: Yucatán
items.note: This is an older Yucatán plate design, used approximately from 2016 to 2019, and commonly found in the older Street View coverage of the state. The plate is white with a thick green stripe along the top and a thinner green stripe along the bottom. The contrast between the bold upper stripe and the subtle lower line makes it fairly straightforward to identify.

items.name: Zacatecas
items.note: This is the newest Zacatecas plate design, introduced in 2022, and is widely found throughout the current Street View coverage of the state. The plate is predominantly white and red. When blurred, it displays a thick red stripe along the bottom that features a distinctive mountain shape, which can sometimes resemble a triangle. This uniquely shaped stripe is the key detail to remember once you familiarize yourself with its silhouette, this plate becomes quite recognizable.

collections.title: Australia – states & territories
collections.intro: Plates are only slightly visible through the blur, so learn the dominant colours.

items.name: ACT
items.note: The ACT plate features equally sized blue sections on both sides with a white area in the center. This symmetry helps distinguish it from the Tasmania plate, which has more blue concentrated on the right side. For comparison, Tasmania plate on next slide.

items.name: NSW
items.note: The easiest to recognize is the New South Wales plate, which appears purely yellow when blurred, making it easily identifiable even from a distance.

items.name: NSW
items.note: The New South Wales black and white plate appears slightly darker than the South Australia plate when blurred. Since both can look similar, pay attention to the surroundings—yellow plates are more common in NSW. For comparison, SA plate on next slide.

items.name: NT
items.note: The Northern Territory plate features a bright red text on white design, similar to Queensland’s, but in a slightly lighter red. For distinction, look at the surroundings — the NT often has dry, reddish soil and sparse vegetation, giving off a distinct outback vibe compared to Queensland’s greener and more tropical feel. For comparison, Queensland plate on next slide.

items.name: Queensland
items.note: The Queensland plate is very similar to the Northern Territory one, but uses a darker shade of red. For distinction, rely on the surrounding environment — Queensland usually feels more humid and lush, while the Northern Territory tends to look drier and more outback-like. For comparison, NT plate on next slide.

items.name: SA
items.note: The South Australia plate is purely black and white. When blurred, it often appears black on the sides with a small white 'dot' in the center, though in certain lighting conditions it can also look entirely white. It can look like the black and white NSW plate but in a lighter white when blurred: For comparison, NSW plate on next slide.

items.name: Tasmania
items.note: The Tasmania plate typically has more blue concentrated on the right side, while the ACT plate shows symmetrical blue sections on both sides. This subtle difference can help tell them apart when the image is blurred. For comparison, ACT plate on next slide.

items.name: Victoria
items.note: The Victoria plate is easy to recognize thanks to its distinctive blue triangle in the center, which appears as a blue dot in the upper middle of the plate when blurred.

items.name: WA
items.note: One of the easiest to recognize is the Western Australia plate, which features a blue horizontal bar across the top. This element remains clearly visible even when the plate is blurred.

collections.title: Japan – utility pole plates by region
collections.intro: Not car plates: the plate on a utility pole shows which regional power company the area belongs to.

items.name: Chubu
items.note: Chubu plate is super unique because of the rounded shape, you can spot it from far away.

items.name: Chugoku
items.note: Chugoku plates will have usually written Energia in latin and sometimes they will include logo.

items.name: Hokkaido
items.note: Hokkaido plate can be recognized by having a lot of numbers in rows of 2.

items.name: Hokuriku
items.note: Silver horizontal plates with logo on the top right. NTT plates will be also horizontal(in Tohoku NTT plates are vertical, and only Tohoku plate is horizontal).

items.name: Kansai
items.note: One of the hardest plate to recognize. Have different designs but will have Japanese written in the middle/or the right and then characters below it in rows of 2 and will usually have 2 numbers at the bottom left/right.

items.name: Kanto
items.note: Often silver and handwritten characters. Horizontal characters above three vertical digits.

items.name: Kyushu
items.note: Distinc logo(sometimes might be missing). Three numbers horizontally near the top, with 4 vertical characters below them on the right(1 kana and 3 numbers).

items.name: Okinawa
items.note: Plate with multiple numbers and lines in between them. Often will have more than 2 plates.

items.name: Shikoku
items.note: Distinct logo that you can remember since it has 4 dots representing 4 prefectures of Shikoku.

items.name: Tohoku
items.note: Silver horizontal plates with logo in top left. NTT plate will be vertical.(In Hokuriku all the plates will be horizontal)

collections.title: World – country plates
collections.intro: One typical plate per country with how to tell it from its look-alikes.

items.name: Albania
items.note:
Albanian licence plates either have blue strips on both sides or a single red strip on the left side.

NOTE: Albania is the only European country with red on the left side of the licence plate. Furthermore, Italian licence plates also have blue strips on both sides, however Italian front plates are distinctly shorter.

items.name: Argentina
items.note:
Argentina uses two types of licence plates: a black one, which will be visible on street view with a black dot in the middle, and a white one with a blue bar at the top.

NOTE: The black dot can only be found on Argentinian licence plates, while the blue bar can be found in Brazil as well.

items.name: Austria
items.note:
Austria has long, white licence plates with the standard blue EU strip on the left. But has a tiny bit of red around it aswell as on the left side, can often be hard to see.

Most useful for distinguishing Austria from Germany which has just the default EU plate.

items.name: Bangladesh
items.note:
Bangladeshi licence plates are either white, black or turquoise.

NOTE: The turquoise plate can only be found in Bangladesh.

items.name: Belgium
items.note: Licence plates in Belgium use red text. You can recognise this distinct colour even through the blur.

items.name: Bhutan
items.note:
Licence plates in Bhutan are almost always red and can easily be seen on vehicles.

NOTE: Within Asia, Bhutan is the only country that uses full red licence plates.

items.name: Bolivia
items.note:
Bolivia has short, white licence plates with blue text. The blue text can be hard to see through the blur, so plates might appear as plain white.

Most useful for distinguishing Bolivia from Peru which has either white or yellow license plates.

items.name: Botswana
items.note:
Botswana has white front plates and yellow rear plates, similar to UK-style plates.

NOTE: Botswana and Namibia are the only countries in southern Africa where yellow rear plates are predominantly found.

items.name: Brazil
items.note: Licence plates in Brazil were white until 2018. Now, a white plate with a blue stripe on top is used. Red is still used for commercial vehicles.

items.name: Chile
items.note:
Regular vehicles have white licence plates, while commercial and taxi vehicles have orange plates.

NOTE: Orange plates can also be seen in Ecuador. Brazilian commercial plates are red, but can look similar in some lighting.

items.name: Colombia
items.note:
Colombian licence plates are typically yellow.

NOTE: Within South America, yellow licence plates are almost exclusively found in Colombia.

items.name: Costa Rica
items.note:
Costa Rican licence plates are typically short and white, with blue text, giving it a light blue tint through the blur.

Super useful for distinguishing Costa Rica from Panama.

items.name: Cyprus
items.note: Cyprus uses both standard white European license plates, and UK-style plates that have a yellow rear plate. Most license plates have the EU strip on the left. Rental cars, which have a distinct red plate, are not uncommon either.

items.name: Denmark
items.note:
Standard plates are long and white, with a blue strip on the left. Commercial plates are yellow. And so-called “Parrot” plates have a yellow section on the left hand side. These are unique to Denmark.

NOTE: The Netherlands, Luxembourg and the UK use yellow plates for private vehicles.

items.name: Dominican Republic
items.note:
DR licence plates are somewhat reminiscent of New Jersey plates, being pale yellow at the top and white at the bottom.

NOTE: The Dominican Republic is the only part of Latin America, apart from Puerto Rico and Panama, where front plates are not required.

Could be usefull in nmpz or if you forgot the Dominican Republic google car.

items.name: France
items.note:
Modern French plates are long and white, with blue strips on both sides of the plate. The left strip will be more visible than the right strip.

Some older French plates lack the right blue strip, with the rear plate being yellow. These are very rare in newer coverage.

NOTE: Italian plates also have two blue strips, which are equally visible. In addition, Italian front plates are considerably shorter.

items.name: Greece
items.note: Greek licence plates are either all white or have the standard European design, with a blue strip on the left side. Taxis have yellow licence plates.

items.name: Hong Kong
items.note: Hong Kong has white front licence plates and yellow rear licence plates. The licence plates can be long or short. Some cars have an additional black mainland Chinese licence plate.

items.name: Iceland
items.note:
Icelandic licence plates are fully white with blue characters. Unlike most of Europe, the plates do not feature a blue strip on the left.

It can be hard to see the blue of the characters through the blur of the plates.

items.name: India
items.note: Indian licence plates are typically fairly long, with the most common design being white. Commercial vehicles typically use yellow plates, while electric vehicles use green.

items.name: Indonesia
items.note:
Indonesian licence plates are black with white letters. The letters usually appear as three white sections through the blur.

Commercial vehicles use yellow licence plates.

Plates in newer coverage can be white too.

NOTE: Malaysian licence plates are also black, but generally have two white sections.

items.name: Israel
items.note:
Israeli licence plates are yellow with a blue strip on the left.

NOTE: While this design is specific for Israel, it is also very common on the West Bank. Jordan and the UAE use white licence plates. Tunisia uses black plates.

items.name: Italy
items.note:
Contrary to most European licence plates, Italian plates have blue strips on either side of the plate. Furthermore, the front plate is distinctly shorter than most European plates, which in combination with the two strips, makes it unique.

NOTE: Albanian licence plates also have two blue strips, and French licence plates have a smaller strip on the right. However, neither Albanian nor French front plates are short.

items.name: Japan
items.note: Japan uses a standard short white licence plate with green text. You will often see a different short yellow version with black text issued to “light automobiles”, otherwise known as Kei Cars.

items.name: Kenya
items.note: Kenya uses long white front licence plates. The rear counterpart is square and yellow.

items.name: Laos
items.note:
Laotian licence plates are short and yellow. This distinguishes them from nearby Thailand and Cambodia, who both use white plates on non-commercial vehicles.

Laotian commercial plates are white, and government plates are blue.

NOTE: Thailand uses yellow plates for commercial vehicles, such as taxis.

items.name: Lebanon
items.note: Standard Lebanese licence plates are either long with a blue strip on the left, similar to most licence plates in Europe, or short with a similar blue strip on the left or above, which makes it unique. Licence plates on taxis are notably deep red. You may also find licence plates with other colours.

items.name: Liechtenstein
items.note: Liechtenstein uses black plates with white lettering and a yellow-and-red emblem near the left side. When blurred, the plates will appear grey, with the emblem colours being visible.

items.name: Luxembourg
items.note:
Luxembourg uses long yellow plates with a blue strip on the left.

Since Luxembourg is a small country, foreign cars with white plates are somewhat common.

NOTE: There are only a few other European countries that use yellow plates for private vehicles:

The Netherlands has yellow plates front and rear.

The UK has yellow rear plates.

Some pre-2009 French cars have yellow rear plates.

items.name: Malaysia
items.note:
Malaysian licence plates are black and generally have two white sections. These are visible even when blurred.

NOTE: Indonesian licence plates are also black, but they will have three white sections.

items.name: Malta
items.note: Like most of Europe, Maltese licence plates have a blue strip on the left. However, unlike most of Europe, short plates are very common.

items.name: Mexico
items.note:
Mexico uses short licence plates with a large variety of designs. Front plates are required.

NOTE: For an overview of the most common regional designs, see this image.

items.name: Montenegro
items.note:
Montenegro uses the standard European plate with a blue strip, and the Montenegro coat of arms on a red circle. The red circle is visible through the blur.

NOTE: The white section of Albanian licence plates do not have a red circle.

items.name: Namibia
items.note:
Namibia primarily uses yellow front and back licence plates. Vanity plates are white, with blue lettering.

NOTE: Botswana and Namibia are the only countries in southern Africa where yellow rear plates are predominantly found.

items.name: Nepal
items.note:
Nepali licence plates are typically fairly long, with the most common design being white. Private vehicles use red plates, while public vehicles use black ones.

Very usefull for distinguishing Nepal from India.

items.name: Netherlands
items.note:
The Netherlands has long, yellow licence plates with the standard European blue strip on the left. Dutch taxis have blue plates.

NOTE: The only other countries in Europe with yellow licence plates are Luxembourg and the UK. For the UK, only the back plates are yellow, and they often lack the blue strip. In addition, some older coverage in France features the French yellow back plates. In Denmark, you can find yellow plates on commercial vehicles.

items.name: New Zealand
items.note:
New Zealand uses white licence plates with black text, which appears mostly white through the blur.

NOTE: Some vehicles have custom licence plates which make the sides of the licence plate appear blue or black.

Most useful for distinguishing New Zealand from certain Australia states

items.name: Nigeria
items.note:
Nigeria uses short licence plates that appear somewhat green through the blur.

Could be useful if the police car isnt visible.

items.name: North Macedonia
items.note:
North Macedonian licence plates are white and sometimes have the standard European blue strip on the left. They also have a noticeable red block near the left side of the licence plate.

NOTE: Serbia will almost always have a blue strip on their licence plates.

items.name: Norway
items.note:
Norway has long white licence plates with the standard European strip on the left.

Commercial plates are green. These are often seen on vans.

NOTE: Within Europe, green licence plates are most commonly seen in Norway, but can also be found on electric vehicles in several other countries.

items.name: Oman
items.note: Licence plates on private vehicles are generally yellow, while commercial vehicles have red plates.

items.name: Panama
items.note:
Panama features short licence plates, most commonly white with a horizontal turquoise strip on the top. Rarely, the strip can have other colours.

Front plates are not required in Panama.

Super useful for distinguishing Panama from Costa Rica

items.name: Peru
items.note:
Peruvian licence plates are either white or yellow. In contrast to the white plates, yellow plates are less likely to be seen.

Additionally, taxis in Peru typically use licence plates that are yellow on the top and white on the bottom. A white plate with a yellow stripe on top of the license plate are also seen on taxis, New Jersey and Dominican Republic have this design too.

NOTE: Within South America, yellow licence plates are only found in Peru, Colombia and rarely, Chile.

items.name: philippines
items.note: Standard white licence plates with black text are used for passenger vehicles. You can also find many that are privately issued, which are recognizable due to their green tint, which is actually quite common to see.

items.name: Portugal
items.note:
Portuguese plates are long and white, with a blue strip on the left. Most plates have a yellow strip on the right, which is unique to Portugal.

The yellow strip was discontinued in 2020, so in Generation 4 coverage you may sometimes see plates with just the blue strip.

items.name: Qatar
items.note: Regular cars in Qatar have long, white licence plates with a maroon strip on the left. Trucks have square, black licence plates and police plates are blue.

items.name: Russia
items.note:
Russian licence plates are fully white with black text.

NOTE: Most European counterparts will feature a blue strip on the left hand side.

items.name: Rwanda
items.note: Rwanda uses long white front and yellow back licence plates.

items.name: San Marino
items.note:
San Marino licence plates are short, white and have blue lettering on them. The red R can also often be seen through the blur.

NOTE: Other European countries will typically have longer licence plates, often with one or more blue strips.

items.name: Senegal
items.note: Senegal is the only African country to use fully blue licence plates. A newer version exists in Generation 4 which looks like the standard European licence plate which is white with a blue strip on the left.

items.name: Sri Lanka
items.note: Vehicles in Sri Lanka have long white front plates and short yellow rear plates.

items.name: Switzerland
items.note:
Swiss license plates differ substantially from other European plates. They are fully white and lack the blue strip found in most other European countries.

Front plates are extremely short compared to most in Europe.

Rear plates can be either long or tall. In both cases the red country emblem can be seen on the left, while the canton emblem can be seen on the right.

items.name: Tunisia
items.note:
Tunisian licence plates are black with white text.

NOTE: Military plates feature a small Tunisian flag on the left side of the plate, which is visible on the dark green follow car.

items.name: Ukraine
items.note:
Ukraine uses long, white licence plates, with a distinctive blue and yellow strip on the left (the colours of the flag).

You may also come across older plates, where the blue and yellow are difficult to spot.

NOTE: Russia uses fully white licence plates, without a strip on the left.

items.name: United Kingdom
items.note: Similar to the United Kingdom, the Isle of Man uses white front licence plates with yellow rears, but with a red strip on the left.

items.name: United Kingdom
items.note:
UK front plates are white, while back plates are yellow. Some plates have a blue strip on the left, but most do not.

Additionally, you might see a plate with a green ‘Zero Emissions’ strip.

NOTE: Ireland uses white front and back plates, always with a blue strip on the left.

items.name: Uruguay
items.note:
Uruguayan licence plates are plain white with black characters.

NOTE: Neighbouring Argentina also uses white licence plates, but they will have either a black dot in the middle or a blue bar at the top.
